description: Na₂BeCl₄ is Spinel-like structured and crystallizes in the orthorhombic Pnma space group. There are two inequivalent Na¹⁺ sites. In the first Na¹⁺ site, Na¹⁺ is bonded to six Cl¹⁻ atoms to form NaCl₆ octahedra that share corners with eight NaCl₆ octahedra, corners with four equivalent BeCl₄ tetrahedra, edges with two equivalent NaCl₆ octahedra, and  an edgeedge with one BeCl₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 52-66°. There are a spread of Na-Cl bond distances ranging from 2.75-2.83 Å. In the second Na¹⁺ site, Na¹⁺ is bonded to six Cl¹⁻ atoms to form NaCl₆ octahedra that share corners with four equivalent NaCl₆ octahedra, corners with two equivalent BeCl₄ tetrahedra, edges with four NaCl₆ octahedra, and edges with two equivalent BeCl₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 57-66°. There are a spread of Na-Cl bond distances ranging from 2.72-2.83 Å. Be²⁺ is bonded to four Cl¹⁻ atoms to form BeCl₄ tetrahedra that share corners with six NaCl₆ octahedra and edges with three NaCl₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 50-58°. There is one shorter (2.01 Å) and three longer (2.05 Å) Be-Cl bond lengths. There are three inequivalent Cl¹⁻ sites. In the first Cl¹⁻ site, Cl¹⁻ is bonded in a distorted rectangular see-saw-like geometry to three Na¹⁺ and one Be²⁺ atom. In the second Cl¹⁻ site, Cl¹⁻ is bonded in a rectangular see-saw-like geometry to three Na¹⁺ and one Be²⁺ atom. In the third Cl¹⁻ site, Cl¹⁻ is bonded in a rectangular see-saw-like geometry to three Na¹⁺ and one Be²⁺ atom.
